families.name: Extraction
families.definition: Extract entities or values explicitly stated in text, tables, or figures.

families.name: Attribution
families.definition: Identify the source, requester, author, or communicator of information.
examples: Who sent Nora Bell's welcome email?

families.name: Computation
families.definition: Apply question-specified calculations to recorded values.
examples: How much does the deficit-to-GDP share increase?

families.name: Comparison
families.definition: Compare results or properties to identify differences, rankings, or choices.
examples: Which frame setting fits the latency budget?

families.name: Interpretation
families.definition: Draw conclusions or assess claims using recorded evidence.
examples: Do the counts support a 12-risk increase?

families.name: Cross-source
families.definition: Identify conflicting information across records or determine which value applies.
examples: Which action-log deadline applies after the correction?

families.name: Temporal
families.definition: Identify information at a specified time or trace its revisions.

families.name: Unanswerability
families.definition: Identify missing information or unsupported premises.
examples: What is the measured serving cost?
